# #129 — Make OpenBrain the required Hermes memory authority

State: CLOSED
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-06-18T06:11:22Z
Updated: 2026-06-18T10:59:15Z
Closed: 2026-06-18T10:59:15Z

---

## Problem
The OpenBrain Hermes plugin is meant to fully replace anything old local memory was supposed to do. It must not be optional, advisory, or one provider among several. OpenBrain is the durable memory authority for Hermes agents.

## Scope
Define and enforce OB Required Mode for rtech-hermes deployments.

## Requirements
- Active Hermes config for opted-in agents must have memory.provider=openbrain, memory_enabled=true, user_profile_enabled=true.
- Startup/update verification must fail if OpenBrain provider is missing, disabled, incompatible, or not the active memory provider.
- No fallback memory provider semantics for opted-in agents.
- All explicit memory writes, turn events, compaction checkpoints, recall, and replay/spool behavior route through OpenBrain.
- Remove or correct stale docs/config examples that imply old local-memory responsibilities still exist outside OpenBrain.

## Acceptance Criteria
- scripts/update.sh or a dedicated verifier fails when OpenBrain is not the sole active memory provider for opted-in agents.
- Tests cover disabled/misconfigured provider cases.
- Live rollout canary proves OpenBrain handles memory read/write/checkpoint behavior for at least one opted-in agent.
